name: dbx
description: 25 MB lightweight cross-platform database client for 100+ databases, including MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis, MongoDB, DuckDB, SQL Server, and Dameng. Built-in AI, MCP Server, CLI, desktop and Docker.
one_liner: A tiny, all-in-one app for browsing and editing almost any type of database, with a built-in AI assistant to write the queries for you.
buyer: A freelance backend developer or small dev shop juggling several clients' different databases (MySQL, Postgres, Mongo) who wants one lightweight tool instead of paying for TablePlus or DataGrip licenses per teammate.
business_use_cases: A freelance developer manages every client's database from one 25MB app instead of installing a separate tool per database engine.
A small dev agency standardizes new hires on dbx so onboarding to a client's stack (whatever database it uses) takes minutes, not a license request.
A no-code agency uses the built-in AI assistant to let non-technical staff safely query client databases in plain English.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a paid 'teams' tier with shared connection profiles and audit logs for agencies.
Sell a premium AI-query add-on with a more capable model for complex query generation.

steal_this: This weekend, package dbx with a preset connection profile and a cheat-sheet as a 'starter database toolkit' for freelancers just picking up their first client project.
